Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaComm Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as background noise may be transmitted. Today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaComm's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments across our telecommunications and media operations.

Our key achievements include optimizing our spectrum assets with high utilization rates and clear plans for future allocations to support 5G expansion and media delivery. We've made significant progress in 5G deployment, alongside targeted network investments that are enhancing coverage and performance. Our content and media segment has delivered impressive revenue growth, profitability improvements, and subscriber gains through bundling synergies. Financially, we've generated robust free cash flow, maintained strong EBITDA margins with upward guidance, guided capex prudently toward high-return network projects, ensured dividend sustainability, and kept leverage ratios healthy amid debt management.

The launch of NovaStream Ultra, our next-gen streaming bundle integrated with 5G fixed wireless access, is exceeding expectations, resulting in 1.2 million net subscriber adds and a 15% uplift in blended ARPU. Further milestones are strong postpaid phone growth and fiber passings expansion. We are also focusing on AI-driven personalization in content delivery. Our dedication to operational efficiencies and sustainability is bearing fruit with opex savings and green initiatives. Our strategy is to enhance converged telecom-media offerings. We are actively investing in edge computing and Open RAN for cost efficiencies. We are also exploring enterprise private networks and finally, analyzing regulatory opportunities like BEAD funding to bridge the digital divide.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $18.5 billion, reflecting a 6% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $7.0 billion, resulting in a margin of 37.8%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $4.2 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Before I dive deeper into the quarter's financials, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our spectrum assets, which remain the crown jewel of our telecommunications and media strategy at NovaComm. Spectrum is the lifeblood of our wireless operations, powering everything from our nationwide 5G Standalone network to fixed wireless access broadband and low-latency media delivery for streaming services like NovaStream. With data consumption up 28% year-over-year in Q3, driven by 5G video streaming, cloud gaming, and enterprise IoT, we're maximizing utilization while preparing for future capacity needs.

Our current spectrum portfolio includes about 420 MHz of average mid-band spectrum across our top 100 markets, featuring prime C-band holdings from FCC Auction 107 totaling 280 MHz, paired with 160 MHz of low-band in the 600 MHz range from the 2021 incentive auction, and over 1.2 GHz of mmWave in 45 top metros, deployed with Nokia and Ericsson small cells. This positions us competitively, with mid-band depth matching Verizon's and higher urban weighting than T-Mobile's.

Utilization has risen to 78% overall in Q3, up from 62% last year, with spectral efficiency at 4.2 bits/Hz via advanced MIMO and AI traffic steering. Low-band is at 85%, supporting 40% of rural coverage and 2.8 million FWA households; mid-band at 72%, delivering 450 Mbps speeds with 35% YoY traffic growth, 22% from NovaStream; mmWave at 55% but 12 bits/Hz efficiency, boosted 25% by Dynamic Spectrum Sharing. Northeast metros hit 92% peak, Midwest 68%, rural Sunbelt 52%. Throughput per MHz is up 22% QoQ to 18 Mbps/MHz, but we project 85-90% utilization by year-end.

To optimize, we've implemented AI-powered spectrum orchestration on our NovaRAN Open RAN platform with Mavenir, shifting traffic dynamically for 18% efficiency gains; network slicing dedicates 15% of C-band for media with 99.9999% uptime, cutting congestion 12%; and 5CC carrier aggregation for 80% of subs, pushing 1.2 Gbps peaks and 4% ARPU lift. These deferred $450 million in capex while maintaining a Net Promoter Score of 62.

For the future, our $8.2 billion 2025 capex allocates 35% or $2.9 billion to spectrum: refarming 30 MHz PCS for 5G SA and 10% low-band for NB-IoT targeting $500 million enterprise revenue; $1.5 billion for FCC Auction 112 CBRS expansion; $800 million for 25,000 mmWave nodes with AWS private 5G; and 5% for 6G sub-THz R&D with Qualcomm and NYU. This strengthens our hybrid moat, with NovaStream's 45 million subs 60% on 5G yielding 25% higher content margins. We'll close gaps with peers via FWA to 10 million lines by 2027, mitigating satellite interference with beamforming. This supports 5-7% wireless revenue growth and 48% EBITDA margins.

Turning to broader financials, we've generated strong free cash flow. In Q3, free cash flow was $2.8 billion, up 18% YoY and beating guidance by $250 million; nine months at $7.9 billion, up 22%, on track for $10.5 billion full-year. Levered FCF was $2.1 billion. Drivers include 5% wireless revenue growth to $14.2 billion with ARPU at $52.30; 12% broadband growth from XGS-PON; and $2.1 billion media from GTM Play's 45 million subs. Operating cash flow hit $4.9 billion on 42.5% EBITDA margins and $350 million savings from RAN virtualization and AI churn models at 0.92%.

Capex was $2.1 billion or 14% of revenues, down 5% YoY: $1.2 billion wireless, $650 million FTTx, $250 million media CDN. Full-year $8.5-9 billion. Utilization: $3.2 billion debt reduction to 2.1x net debt/EBITDA; $2.8 billion shareholder returns with dividend up 7% to $0.65/share and $1.9 billion buybacks; $1.5 billion growth like $800 million C-band and content M&A. North America drove 72%, Europe 18%, APAC 10%.

On capex guidance, full-year 2024 is $18.2-18.8 billion, up 3%, with network at $12.5-13.0 billion or 68%, up 5%: $6.8-7.1 billion 5G including C-band at 85% deployment and mmWave; $3.2-3.4 billion fiber to 15 million locations; $1.5-1.6 billion edge/media; $1.0 billion R&D/sustainability. U.S. 55%, Europe 25%. This yields 2-3% 2025 revenue growth and 42% margins.

For network investments, Q3 capex was $2.8 billion, YTD $7.9 billion up 12%, 45% or $1.26 billion to 5G. Full-year $11.5-12.0 billion total, $4.8 billion 5G; 2025 $10.5-11.0 billion at 18% intensity. We've upgraded 85% macro sites or 65,000, 95% top 100 markets coverage for 280 million people; 60% SA traffic with cloud core; ORAN trials on 5,000 cells saving 18%. U.S. 1.2 Gbps speeds, 2.5 million FWA; Europe 75%; APAC high coverage. 5G subs 55% base or 48 million at 28% higher margins.

Content and media revenue was $2.85 billion, up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ: $1.92 billion subs up 15%, $650 million ads up 8%, $280 million licensing. 48.2 million subs, +1.9 million net adds, 1.1% churn, $12.75 ARPU. EBITDA $925 million at 32.5% margin from efficiencies and bundling. North America 85%, Europe 10%, APAC/LatAm 5%. Initiatives like AI personalization, FAST channels, $2.5 billion content slate; Q4 guide 2.0-2.3 million adds, 11-13% revenue growth.

On EBITDA margins, Q3 was 36.2% up 140 bps; Q4 guide 37-39%; FY25 raised to 38-40%. Tailwinds: opex savings from slicing/Open RAN, wireless 42%, broadband 38%, media 30-32%. Headwinds managed like labor and auctions.

Dividend sustainability: Quarterly $0.50/share, annual $2.00, 4.5% yield; 2.9x FCF coverage from $5.2 billion TTM FCF; 58% payout. Total yield 7.8% with $2.1 billion buybacks. FY24 FCF $5.5-6.0 billion funds $6 billion returns.

Debt: Gross $48.2 billion down 3.8%, net $43.4 billion; 2.8x leverage improved from 3.2x. 65% fixed at 4.1% cost; ratings BBB+/Baa1. Refinancing, asset sales delevering to 2.6x YE24.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage to 95% in top markets, delivering faster speeds averaging 450 Mbps and lower latency under 10ms in SA mode. Our network reliability is at 99.999%, and we're optimizing infrastructure with Open RAN and virtualization for growing demand from video and IoT. Cybersecurity enhancements include AI threat detection across edge nodes. We are committed to sustainable builds, powering 40% of sites with solar and pursuing BEAD grants for rural FWA.

David Kim: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've added 850,000 postpaid phones and 500,000 broadband subs, with total wireless at 85 million and broadband passings at 55%. Customer satisfaction is high with NPS 62, improved via app personalization and bundles. Partnerships with studios and hyperscalers expand offerings like NovaStream zero-rated on 5G. We are prioritizing FWA growth to 10 million lines, capturing rural share against cable and satellite.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are driving innovation with AI and ML for network automation, chatbots slashing service times 30%, and new services like AR/VR streaming slices. R&D investments target 6G prototypes and edge AI. Our technological direction is Open RAN scaling to 30% by 2025 and 5G-Advanced for 10x efficiency.

Raj Singh: Thank you. Operationally, we're boosting efficiency with data analytics for resource optimization and predictive maintenance cutting downtime 20%. Sustainability efforts reduced energy use 18% via green sites. Our operational focus is converging ops for telecom-media, streamlining supply chains with dual vendors.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Emily. Our content strategy centers on converged bundles leveraging our 5G network for low-latency delivery, with $2.5 billion FY24 spend on 15 originals like sci-fi thrillers co-produced internationally. We're expanding FAST to 50+ channels and AI personalization to 90% of users, boosting engagement 25%. Bundling with 65% wireless overlap drives $18.50 ARPU for bundlers. Impact: Q4 2.0-2.3 million net adds, positioning media at 25% of group EBITDA by FY25.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Reyes with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Reyes: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 10 million FWA lines by 2027?

David Kim: Great question, John. We're targeting the digital divide via $1.2 billion BEAD allocation for 65% rural coverage, deploying FWA CPE with 1.2 Gbps speeds and 1.5% churn. Partnerships with municipalities mirror fiber successes, with subsidies competing Starlink. Roadmap: 2.8 million households now, scaling to 10 million through CBRS expansion and low-band optimization, eroding cable share with 45% take rates.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including dividend growth?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Lisa. Priorities: growth capex at 55% wireless/media, then deleveraging to sub-2.5x, and returns. $10.5 billion FY24 FCF covers $1.9 billion dividends with 3% hike to $0.65/share, $3 billion buybacks under $15 billion authorization, $1.1 billion debt paydown. Total 8-9% yield, 2.9x coverage, opportunistic below 8x EV/EBITDA.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Hargrove with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Hargrove: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Sarah Thompson: Regulatory navigation is key. We're advocating at WRC-27 for mid-band expansions, pursuing FCC auctions like 112 with $1.5 billion budget deployable fast. For net neutrality, hedged via backhaul diversity; EU Gigabit mandates unlock grants. BEAD pursuits worth $3 billion, and we're compliant with price caps while pushing enterprise slicing.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
